items.text: President Trump announced at 2:00 p.m. that Mesabi Metallics, owned by India-based Essar Group, plans a $15 billion steel mill in eastern Iowa, using ore from its mine near Nashwauk, Minnesota.
items.detail: The mill would use iron ore from Mesabi Metallics' mine on Minnesota's Iron Range, which opened this month and plans 350 full-time jobs. No construction timeline or mill job count was given.
items.why: A $15 billion private investment in U.S. steel capacity. Rated 3 rather than higher because it is a plan, not yet under construction.

items.text: A federal judge held the administration in contempt for deporting an asylum seeker in violation of court orders.
items.detail: A contempt finding means the court concluded the government violated its orders. The asylum seeker was deported while those orders were in place.
items.why: A federal court finding that the executive branch defied court orders bears on the limits of executive power.

items.text: The White House announced a U.S.-China dialogue on AI, including a direct communication channel for incidents.
items.detail: The channel lets the two governments communicate directly to defuse incidents involving artificial intelligence.
items.why: A formal U.S.-China line on AI incidents between the two leading AI powers; it creates no binding rules.

items.text: The administration has committed $307 million of the $400 million in Ukraine aid Congress approved, with a September 30 deadline.
items.detail: Congress approved $400 million. $307 million had been committed as of the latest report, with a September 30 deadline.
items.why: Concerns money already approved; the practical question is whether the remaining $93 million is committed by the deadline.

items.text: Russian attacks on Ukraine killed at least 12 people over the weekend, including 7 in Kyiv.
items.detail: Seven of those killed, including a child, were in Kyiv. Russian drones also hit the headquarters of Kyivstar, a Ukrainian telecom company.
items.why: Deadly attacks in an ongoing war. Rated 3 because they continue an existing pattern rather than marking a new phase.

items.text: President Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the war.
items.detail: Iran had offered terms to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a major route for global oil shipments, and end the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, now in its seventh month.
items.why: Determines whether an active war involving the U.S. continues and whether a key global oil route reopens.

items.text: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran is waiting for an official U.S. response before ending ceasefire talks; an Iranian official said Iran will not change its position on its nuclear program.
items.detail: The statements followed the U.S. rejection of Iran's proposal. An Iranian army spokesman also said Iran's forces are prepared for renewed U.S. attacks.
items.why: Shows where ceasefire talks stand, but is a statement of position, not a decision or action.

items.text: The Supreme Court rejected a request from Missouri Republicans concerning the state's congressional map.
items.detail: The dispute concerns how Missouri's U.S. House districts are drawn. The Court declined the request from state Republicans.
items.why: District maps set the boundaries for U.S. House races in the state, but the decision is limited to Missouri.

items.text: The Supreme Court ruled the administration can use a citizenship verification system to check voter eligibility.
items.detail: The ruling allows the federal government's citizenship verification system to be used when checking whether registered voters are eligible.
items.why: A Supreme Court decision that applies nationwide to voter eligibility checks ahead of the midterm elections.

items.text: President Trump moved to withhold $800 million in spending Congress approved for immigration, race-related and education programs.
items.detail: The money had already been approved by Congress for programs related to immigration, race and education.
items.why: Affects $800 million in approved federal spending and Congress's control over how funds are spent.

items.text: A classified U.S. assessment found Saudi Arabia has kept open the option of developing a nuclear weapon.
items.detail: The finding comes from a classified U.S. intelligence assessment reported this week.
items.why: Bears on the risk of nuclear weapons spreading in the Middle East during an active regional war.

items.text: Swiss voters rejected a proposal for stricter national neutrality.
items.detail: The proposal, which Russia supported, would have tightened Switzerland's neutrality rules.

items.text: The White House announced it is reversing prior federal restrictions on domestic mining.
items.detail: The White House said the change reverses earlier federal restrictions on domestic mining.
items.why: A policy change for the mining sector. Rated 2 because the specific rule changes and their scope were not detailed.

items.text: President Trump called on Congress to pass legislation on college sports.
items.detail: The President asked Congress to pass legislation governing college sports.
items.why: A request to Congress, not a law or an order.

items.text: The new U.S.-China Board of Trade announced $60 billion in reciprocal tariff cuts. Soybeans are not included.
items.detail: The U.S.-China Board of Trade announced the cuts on September 27. Soybeans, a major U.S. export to China, are not included.
items.why: $60 billion in tariff changes between the world's two largest economies affects prices, importers and exporters.
